There's an awful lot of misunderstanding of the "Balanced Budget and Emergency Deficit Control Act of 1985" going around.

The invoking of it isn't some magical power that let's the President do what he wants. It's always invoked in budgets anymore, because the act placed a cap on discretionary spending above a certain limit, that if Congress can't agree on, funds automatically get sequestered. So every Omnibus Bill, because they're always over the cap and thus adjusting the cap as part of the budget, invokes it.

The idea that President Trump can use "discretionary spending" however he wants is just wrong. Most of the budget is discretionary spending. There's mandatory expenditures and discretionary spending. The discretionary part just means there's not other legislature mandating that they meet it.

Mandatory spending (e.g. entitlements) such as Social Security where they are otherwise mandated to spend that much regardless of budget. For example they could come across and discover that no where near as many people died as they thought would, thus Social Security costs will be much higher than previously thought. Doesn't matter, they have to spend it because they're otherwise mandated to - can't just tell the people they planned on dying, "Too bad you're not getting it." Anything that falls along those lines of entitlements is mandatory spending.

Discretionary spending is everything else. "Hey, we don't have enough money to pay the troops in this budget." "Well, scrap an air platform, or lay off some troops or something, we don't have mandate to have that many troops or equipment." (Not the case in this budget, but an easy example).

While we're at it there's nothing magical about an Omnibus bull vs appropriations either. Theoretically Congress is supposed to pass 12 separate appropriations to do the budget in piece mail. This is supposed to keep federal spending accounts separate, so you couldn't hold up, for example, funding for the military by demanding subsidies for agriculture. Congress being somewhere between incompetent and corrupt threw that out years ago and combined everything into omnibus (which is just fancy speak for doing all twelve as one) so they could do exactly what they're not supposed to and tie everything up.

Long story short there's nothing magical about Omnibus or repeatedly amended Balanced Budget and Emergency Deficit Control Act of 1985.
